section.title: Local linear approximation
section.p: The derivative function provides the best linear model for a function near a point of tangency. Calculus allows us to replace a complicated curved graph by a simple straight line locally.

subsection.title: Sensitivity and propagated error
subsection.p: The derivative serves as a conversion multiplier relating input measurement uncertainties to output errors: dy \approx f'(x)\,dx.

statement.p: For A(r)=\pi r^2, dA = 2\pi r\,dr. The relative error is
A 0.5\% measurement error in radius produces an approximate 1.0\% error in computed area.
For R(x)=\frac{1}{x}, R'(x)=-\frac{1}{x^2}. At x=0.01, R'(0.01)=-10{,}000, meaning a microscopic input error dx=0.0001 induces a large output error dR \approx -1.
